title: LLM price war goes customer-by-customer: OpenAI reportedly offering 90% off to poach Anthropic accounts
subtitle: List prices on frontier models are down roughly 70–80% in months — and The Information says OpenAI is quietly cutting bespoke deals of up to 90% off to pull Anthropic's largest customers away, with Replit and DataCamp named as targets.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Two things happened to frontier-model pricing this month, and they are not the same story. On the published list, Max Woolf's October 25 analysis documents OpenAI cutting GPT-5.6 Luna by 80% in July and Anthropic cutting cache-read costs by 75% with the Fable 5.1 release in September — composite reductions of 70–75% across both labs since summer. OpenAI's flagship Sol input price fell from $5 to $2 per million tokens between June and September. Separately, The Information reported this weekend that OpenAI is offering discounts of up to 90% to specific large Anthropic customers to switch, with Replit and DataCamp named in follow-up coverage. Replit was reportedly offered more than 30% off a contract worth over $100 million a year; DataCamp's CEO said costs fell 80–90% after the switch.

The 90% figure is a negotiated discount, not a published price. The 80% figure is a list cut anyone can read on the pricing page. Both matter, and they interact. List cuts are driven by competitive pressure from Chinese open-weight models — Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro at a third of Opus 5.5's price last week, DeepSeek's $15B war chest, the broader commoditization curve. Negotiated discounts are driven by the fact that OpenAI and Anthropic are, functionally, selling to the same hundred or so companies that account for most of the frontier spend. When your competitor can walk a customer across the street in a weekend, list price stops being the floor; it becomes the sticker. The real price is whatever the enterprise AE wrote on the SOW.

The implication for the labs is uncomfortable. OpenAI's $30 billion bridge round and $1.25 trillion valuation (reported last week) are built on a revenue model that assumes customers will stay as context, memory, and agents deepen the lock-in. Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus (reported October 24 by WSJ) shows an $80.7 billion H1 net loss. Neither company has pricing power. Both are burning capital to keep usage inside their walls while the per-token margin inverts. This is the fourth or fifth 'cheapest smart model yet' cycle of the year, and each one gets closer to the point where frontier inference clears at commodity economics.

A note for learners: list price is a signal; your bill is a negotiation. If you are evaluating providers for anything above hobbyist volume, assume there is a discount on offer that is not posted on the website and ask for it. More important, build your stack so switching the provider is one config change, not a six-month migration. Use the OpenAI-compatible chat completions API shape wherever possible, keep prompts and evals portable, and separate the model call from everything around it. The companies that will benefit most from this price war are the ones that stay cheap to move.
